# Introduction

Missing quantitative-proteomics intensities can follow more than one pattern.
Some values are absent for approximately intensity-independent, MAR-like
reasons. Low-abundance features can instead fall below detection and produce
MNAR-like missingness. A quantified feature can also be present throughout one
condition and absent throughout another. A single label across all samples can
hide that on/off pattern.

ImputeFinder takes unnormalised log2 protein intensities, classifies each
feature separately within each condition, and removes features that lack enough
observations for the intended downstream branch. The result records each state,
cutoff, rescue value, and drop reason. The labels mean **likely MAR** and
**likely MNAR** under an intensity-cutoff rule; they do not establish the true
cause of missingness. ImputeFinder neither normalises nor imputes values.

Bioconductor packages such as
[`DEP`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/DEP),
[`MSnbase`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/MSnbase), and
[`msImpute`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/msImpute) provide broader
proteomics analysis or imputation machinery. ImputeFinder has a narrower role:
it preserves condition-specific state and coordinates separate downstream
branches while returning either an ordinary matrix or a
`SummarizedExperiment`.

Within a pipeline, those states can form an auditable routing layer. MNAR blocks
can enter a detection-limit branch, MAR blocks can enter a relationship-based
branch, and complete blocks can pass through unchanged.

# Installation

Once ImputeFinder is available from a Bioconductor package repository, install
and load it as follows. Installation code is intentionally not evaluated while
building the vignette.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("imputefinder")

library(imputefinder)
```

# Inputs and classification rules

The input must be an ordinary numeric matrix, or a selected numeric assay in a
`SummarizedExperiment`, with named quantitative features such as protein groups,
peptides, or PTM sites in rows and uniquely named samples in columns. Missing
values are `NA`; `NaN` and infinite values are
rejected. Condition labels must align one-to-one with samples. ImputeFinder
trusts the scientific input contract: it does not infer or apply a log
transform, normalisation, centring, or scaling, and it does not reinterpret
zero.

After rescue, each feature-condition block receives exactly one state:

- `complete` - no value is missing.
- `MNAR` - at least one value is missing and the arithmetic mean of observed
    values is below the condition cutoff.
- `MAR` - at least one value is missing, the mean is at or above the cutoff,
    and strictly more than half the samples are observed.
- `insufficient` - the block is on the MAR side of the cutoff but lacks a
    strict observed majority.

The arithmetic mean is deliberate: one strong observation can move a partly
observed block toward the MAR side, and a mean equal to the cutoff is also on
that side. MAR-like downstream methods need relationships among observed
values, so a strict majority provides a minimum amount of within-condition
information. The majority rule applies only to MAR candidates. A sparse,
low-intensity block can remain MNAR because one observation may be the only
available evidence near the detection limit.

A feature is dropped if it is absent globally, `insufficient` in any condition,
or `MNAR` in every condition. Otherwise its complete state matrix is retained,
including mixtures such as MNAR in one condition and complete in another. An
`insufficient` block cannot support a MAR branch, while an all-MNAR feature has
no complete or MAR-like condition to support retention.

```{r classification-workflow, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.7, fig.cap=workflow_caption}
workflow_nodes <- data.frame(
    x = c(0, 1, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 2),
    y = c(3, 3, 3, 1.9, 1.9, 1.9, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
    scope = c(rep("package", 6L), rep("external", 3L)),

        "Drop globally absent\nAnchor fully absent blocks",
        "Profile each condition\nChoose its intensity cutoff",
        "Classify each block\ncomplete / MAR / MNAR\n/ insufficient",
        "Drop whole features\nAny insufficient or\nall conditions MNAR",
        "Return filtered data\nStates + rescue log",

)
```

# Controlled example: mixed missingness across conditions

The motivating examples for ImputeFinder combine three patterns. Missingness
becomes more common as abundance approaches a detection limit, higher-intensity
features can still be missing for approximately random reasons, and a feature
can be undetected in one condition but consistently measured in another. The
controlled panel below places those patterns in one inspectable matrix.

The values are unnormalised log2-like intensities from four control and four
treated samples. Both manual cutoffs are 12. The panel is designed to explain
classification and routing; it does not represent a biological experiment.

```{r manual-fixture}
x <- rbind(
    condition_on_off = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, 16, 17, 16, 18),
    differential_mar = c(14, 15, NA, 16, 20, NA, 21, 22),
    mixed_mechanism = c(8, NA, NA, NA, 15, 16, NA, 17),
    high_tail_mar = c(8, 9, 25, NA, 14, 15, 16, 17),
    sparse_high = c(18, NA, NA, NA, 19, 20, 21, 22),
    all_mnar = c(7.5, NA, NA, NA, 8, NA, NA, NA),
    globally_absent = rep(NA_real_, 8),
    complete_low = c(8, 8, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9),
    complete_high = c(18, 19, 18, 20, 20, 21, 22, 23)
)
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
    sample = c(paste0("control_", 1:4), paste0("treated_", 1:4)),
    condition = rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 4),
    replicate = rep(1:4, times = 2),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
colnames(x) <- sample_metadata$sample
condition <- sample_metadata$condition

fit <- classify_missingness(
    x,
    group = condition,
    cutoffs = c(control = 12, treated = 12),
    seed = 1L
)
fit
```

```{r manual-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=manual_heatmap_caption}
manual_heatmap <- data.frame(
    feature = rep(rownames(x), times = ncol(x)),
    sample = rep(colnames(x), each = nrow(x)),
    intensity = as.vector(x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
manual_heatmap$feature <- factor(
    manual_heatmap$feature,
    levels = rev(rownames(x))
)
manual_heatmap$sample <- factor(
    manual_heatmap$sample,
    levels = colnames(x)
)
manual_heatmap$condition <- factor(
    sample_metadata$condition[
        match(as.character(manual_heatmap$sample), sample_metadata$sample)
    ],
    levels = c("control", "treated"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated")
)
heatmap_sample_labels <- setNames(
    c(paste0("C", 1:4), paste0("T", 1:4)),
    colnames(x)
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    manual_heatmap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = intensity)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = manual_heatmap[is.na(manual_heatmap$intensity), , drop = FALSE],
        mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 4,
        size = 2.1,
        stroke = 0.7,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(
        cols = ggplot2::vars(condition),
        scales = "free_x",
        space = "free_x"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = heatmap_sample_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF",
        high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        name = "log2-like intensity"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Sample", y = "Synthetic protein") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9),
        legend.position = "right"
    )
```

Before classification, a feature missing everywhere is marked `all_missing`
and removed. Every surviving feature fully missing within one condition then
receives one artificial anchor:

1. The minimum finite intensity in each condition is calculated before any
    anchors are inserted.
2. One sample in each fully missing feature-condition block is selected
    uniformly. Selection is with replacement across features.
3. Exactly that cell receives the condition minimum; the others remain `NA`.
4. The feature, condition, selected sample, old and inserted values, and seed
    are recorded.

```{r rescue-log}
fit$seed_log
fit$data["condition_on_off", ]
```

The anchor makes the absent condition classifiable; it is not a completed
imputation. Originally observed cells are preserved exactly. Stable name order
and a local RNG scope make the selected sample reproducible without changing
the global RNG state.

`feature_status` includes every original feature, including dropped rows. The
classification table contains the evidence used to assign each surviving
feature-condition state.

```{r classification-details}
fit$feature_status
fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature %in% c(
        "condition_on_off",
        "mixed_mechanism",
        "high_tail_mar",
        "sparse_high",
        "all_mnar"
    ),
    c("feature", "condition", "observed_count", "missing_count",
        "mean_intensity", "cutoff", "state", "retained", "drop_reason")
]
```

```{r manual-state-map, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5.1, fig.cap=manual_state_caption}
state_features <- setdiff(rownames(x), "globally_absent")
state_plot <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature %in% state_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
state_plot$feature <- factor(
    state_plot$feature,
    levels = rev(state_features)
)
state_plot$condition <- factor(
    state_plot$condition,
    levels = c("control", "treated"),
    labels = c("Control", "Treated")
)
state_plot$state <- factor(
    state_plot$state,
    levels = c("complete", "MAR", "MNAR", "insufficient")
)
status_by_feature <- setNames(
    fit$feature_status$retained,
    fit$feature_status$feature
)
state_feature_labels <- setNames(
    ifelse(
        status_by_feature[state_features],
        state_features,
        paste0(state_features, " (filtered)")
    ),
    state_features
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    state_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = condition, y = feature, fill = state)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = state),
        size = 3.3,
        colour = "#222222"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = state_feature_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            complete = "#D9EAF7",
            MAR = "#DDECCB",
            MNAR = "#FBE3C3",
            insufficient = "#F2C9C9"
        ),
        drop = FALSE,
        name = "State"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Synthetic protein") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "bottom"
    )
```

The examples isolate several decisions in the method. `mixed_mechanism` is MNAR
in control but MAR in treated, so the same feature is routed differently across
conditions. `high_tail_mar` has observed control values of 8, 9, and 25. Its
mean is 14, above the cutoff, and three of four samples are observed. The strong
observation therefore moves the block to MAR, illustrating why the rule uses an
arithmetic mean rather than a median.

`sparse_high` also has a mean above the cutoff, but only one of four control
samples is observed. It is `insufficient` for the MAR branch and is dropped.
`all_mnar` is below the cutoff in both conditions and is dropped because neither
condition supplies a complete or MAR-like block. `complete_low` remains
`complete` despite lying below the cutoff because the cutoff is only needed when
values are missing.

# What pooling conditions would lose

The effect of pooling is easiest to see by applying the same cutoff and majority
rule to `condition_on_off` as one block across all samples. The comparison uses
the original values, before condition-specific rescue.

```{r pooled-comparison}
pooled_values <- unname(x["condition_on_off", ])
pooled_observed <- sum(!is.na(pooled_values))
pooled_mean <- mean(pooled_values, na.rm = TRUE)
pooled_state <- if (all(!is.na(pooled_values))) {
    "complete"
} else if (pooled_mean < 12) {
    "MNAR"
} else if (pooled_observed > length(pooled_values) / 2) {
    "MAR"
} else {
    "insufficient"
}

on_off_states <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$feature == "condition_on_off",
    c("condition", "observed_count", "sample_count", "mean_intensity", "state")
]
on_off_states <- on_off_states[
    match(unique(condition), on_off_states$condition),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
pooled_comparison <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        scope = "Pooled original samples",
        observed_count = pooled_observed,
        sample_count = length(pooled_values),
        mean_intensity = pooled_mean,
        state = pooled_state
    ),
    data.frame(
        scope = paste(on_off_states$condition, "condition"),
        observed_count = on_off_states$observed_count,
        sample_count = on_off_states$sample_count,
        mean_intensity = on_off_states$mean_intensity,
        state = on_off_states$state
    )
)
knitr::kable(
    pooled_comparison,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Scope", "Observed", "Samples", "Mean intensity", "State")
)

on_off_status <- fit$feature_status[
    fit$feature_status$feature == "condition_on_off",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(
    identical(pooled_state, "insufficient"),
    identical(
        on_off_states$state[
            match(c("control", "treated"), on_off_states$condition)
        ],
        c("MNAR", "complete")
    ),
    isTRUE(on_off_status$retained)
)
```

Pooling produces four observations from eight samples. The mean is above the
cutoff, but there is no strict observed majority, so the feature becomes
`insufficient` and would be dropped. Condition-aware classification instead
records the control block as `MNAR`, the treated block as `complete`, and retains
the plausible on/off feature.

# Why downstream imputation remains condition-specific

Condition-aware labels only solve the first part of the problem. The downstream
method must also use donors from the appropriate condition. `differential_mar`
has one missing value in each group, with observed means of 15 in control and 21
in treated. A transparent mean-replacement calculation shows what pooling would
do to that difference.

```{r condition-specific-imputation}
differential_values <- unname(x["differential_mar", ])
condition_means <- vapply(
    c("control", "treated"),
    function(condition_name) {
        mean(
            differential_values[condition == condition_name],
            na.rm = TRUE
        )
    },
    numeric(1L)
)
pooled_replacement <- mean(differential_values, na.rm = TRUE)

within_condition_values <- differential_values
for (condition_name in names(condition_means)) {
    replace_index <- condition == condition_name &
        is.na(within_condition_values)
    within_condition_values[replace_index] <-
        condition_means[[condition_name]]
}
pooled_values <- differential_values
pooled_values[is.na(pooled_values)] <- pooled_replacement

imputation_comparison <- data.frame(
    strategy = c("Within-condition stand-in", "Pooled stand-in"),
    control_replacement = c(condition_means[["control"]], pooled_replacement),
    treated_replacement = c(condition_means[["treated"]], pooled_replacement),
    control_mean = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "control"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "control"])
    ),
    treated_mean = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "treated"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "treated"])
    ),
    difference = c(
        mean(within_condition_values[condition == "treated"]) -
            mean(within_condition_values[condition == "control"]),
        mean(pooled_values[condition == "treated"]) -
            mean(pooled_values[condition == "control"])
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    imputation_comparison,
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c(
        "Strategy",
        "Control replacement",
        "Treated replacement",
        "Control mean",
        "Treated mean",
        "Treated - control"
    )
)

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    imputation_comparison$difference,
    c(6, 4.5),
    tolerance = 1e-12
)))
```

```{r condition-imputation-audit, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=imputation_audit_caption}
imputation_audit_values <- rbind(
    Observed = differential_values,
    `Within-condition stand-in` = within_condition_values,
    `Pooled stand-in` = pooled_values
)
colnames(imputation_audit_values) <- colnames(x)
imputation_inserted <- rbind(rep(FALSE, ncol(x)),
    is.na(differential_values), is.na(differential_values))
imputation_audit <- data.frame(
    strategy = factor(rep(rownames(imputation_audit_values), ncol(x)),
        levels = rev(rownames(imputation_audit_values))),
    sample = factor(rep(colnames(x), each = 3L), levels = colnames(x)),
    condition = factor(rep(condition, each = 3L),
        levels = c("control", "treated"), labels = c("Control", "Treated")),
    intensity = as.vector(imputation_audit_values),
    inserted = as.vector(imputation_inserted)
)
imputation_audit_gaps <- c(
    condition_means[["treated"]] - condition_means[["control"]],
    imputation_comparison$difference
)
imputation_audit_labels <- setNames(paste0(
    rownames(imputation_audit_values), "\nDifference = ", imputation_audit_gaps
), rownames(imputation_audit_values))
ggplot2::ggplot(imputation_audit,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = strategy, fill = intensity)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(data = imputation_audit[imputation_audit$inserted, ],
        fill = NA, colour = "#D55E00", linewidth = 1.2, width = 0.94, height = 0.88) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(data = imputation_audit[!is.na(imputation_audit$intensity), ],
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", intensity), colour = intensity > 18),
        size = 3.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(data = imputation_audit[is.na(imputation_audit$intensity), ],
        shape = 4, size = 2.4, colour = "#555555") +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(cols = ggplot2::vars(condition), scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = heatmap_sample_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = imputation_audit_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0", limits = range(imputation_audit_values, na.rm = TRUE),
        name = "log2-like intensity") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Sample", y = NULL, title = "Inspect what each stand-in inserts") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", colour = NA),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

stopifnot(sum(imputation_inserted) == 4L)
for (strategy in seq_len(nrow(imputation_audit_values))) {
    observed <- !is.na(differential_values)
    stopifnot(identical(unname(imputation_audit_values[strategy, observed]),
        differential_values[observed]))
}
```

The within-condition stand-in preserves the six-unit separation between the
observed group means. The pooled stand-in inserts 18 into both groups and shrinks
that separation to 4.5. Arithmetic-mean replacement is used only to make the
donor-pool effect visible; it is not a recommended MAR algorithm. A
relationship-based method such as k-nearest neighbours can create the same
problem when it borrows information across groups. Impute each routed block
within its condition, then restore the original sample order.

# Real-data case study: Tau phosphosites in human brain

An independent study by
[Wesseling et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.029)
mapped Tau post-translational modifications in post-mortem human control and
Alzheimer's disease tissue. The underlying mass-spectrometry data are available
under PRIDE accession
[PXD020717](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD020717).

This vignette ships a seven-site extract from three control and three
Alzheimer's disease soluble BA46 samples. The values reproduce MaxQuant
`Intensity` columns in the archived `Phospho (STY)Sites.txt` table. Site numbers
follow the P10636-8, 2N4R Tau positions. Zero entries are represented as `NA`,
and positive raw intensities are log2-transformed and rounded to three decimals.
No between-sample normalisation is applied.

The samples and sites were selected to expose several classification states.
Both manual cutoffs are 24.5, chosen for this example rather than copied from the
source study. This compact extract is not intended to estimate a disease effect.
The source repository includes a range-request builder under `data-raw/` that
regenerates the fixture from the public MaxQuant archive.

```{r pxd020717-data}
tau_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "PXD020717_tau_phosphosites.csv",
    package = "imputefinder"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(tau_path))
tau_samples <- utils::read.csv(
    tau_path,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    na.strings = ""
)
tau_features <- grep("^MAPT_", names(tau_samples), value = TRUE)
tau_x <- t(as.matrix(tau_samples[, tau_features, drop = FALSE]))
colnames(tau_x) <- tau_samples$sample
storage.mode(tau_x) <- "double"
tau_condition <- tau_samples$condition

tau_fit <- classify_missingness(
    tau_x,
    group = tau_condition,
    cutoffs = c(control = 24.5, AD = 24.5),
    seed = 1L
)
tau_fit
```

The raw extract shows why a condition-aware label can carry more information
than a pooled label. It also includes incomplete blocks above and below the
manual boundary, complete blocks, one site absent throughout the extract, and
one site that lacks a strict observed majority.

```{r pxd020717-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.6, fig.cap=tau_heatmap_caption}
tau_heatmap <- data.frame(
    feature = rep(rownames(tau_x), times = ncol(tau_x)),
    sample = rep(colnames(tau_x), each = nrow(tau_x)),
    intensity = as.vector(tau_x),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
tau_heatmap$feature <- factor(
    tau_heatmap$feature,
    levels = rev(rownames(tau_x))
)
tau_heatmap$sample <- factor(
    tau_heatmap$sample,
    levels = colnames(tau_x)
)
tau_heatmap$condition <- factor(
    tau_samples$condition[
        match(as.character(tau_heatmap$sample), tau_samples$sample)
    ],
    levels = c("control", "AD"),
    labels = c("Control", "Alzheimer's disease")
)
tau_sample_labels <- setNames(tau_samples$subject, tau_samples$sample)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    tau_heatmap,
    ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature, fill = intensity)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        data = tau_heatmap[is.na(tau_heatmap$intensity), , drop = FALSE],
        mapping = ggplot2::aes(x = sample, y = feature),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 4,
        size = 2.1,
        stroke = 0.7,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(
        cols = ggplot2::vars(condition),
        scales = "free_x",
        space = "free_x"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = tau_sample_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(
        low = "#F7FBFF",
        high = "#08519C",
        na.value = "#E0E0E0",
        name = "log2 intensity"
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Sample", y = "Tau phosphosite") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA

        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),

        legend.position = "right"

```

`MAPT_pS404` is MNAR-like in the selected control samples and complete in the
selected Alzheimer's disease samples. `MAPT_pS202` and `MAPT_pT181` are
MAR-like in both groups. `MAPT_pT403` is MNAR-like in both groups and is filtered.
`MAPT_pT231` is filtered because its control block is above the cutoff but has
only one observed sample. A complete block is classified as complete even when
its mean lies below the cutoff, as shown by `MAPT_pS404` in the Alzheimer's
disease group.

```{r pxd020717-state-map, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap=tau_state_caption}
tau_state_features <- setdiff(rownames(tau_x), "MAPT_pS199")
tau_state_plot <- tau_fit$classifications[
    tau_fit$classifications$feature %in% tau_state_features,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
tau_state_plot$feature <- factor(
    tau_state_plot$feature,
    levels = rev(tau_state_features)
)
tau_state_plot$condition <- factor(
    tau_state_plot$condition,
    levels = c("control", "AD"),
    labels = c("Control", "Alzheimer's disease")
)
tau_state_plot$state <- factor(
    tau_state_plot$state,
    levels = c("complete", "MAR", "MNAR", "insufficient")
)
tau_status_by_feature <- setNames(
    tau_fit$feature_status$retained,
    tau_fit$feature_status$feature
)
tau_state_labels <- setNames(
    ifelse(
        tau_status_by_feature[tau_state_features],
        tau_state_features,
        paste0(tau_state_features, " (filtered)")
    ),
    tau_state_features
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
    tau_state_plot,
    ggplot2::aes(x = condition, y = feature, fill = state)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = state),
        size = 3.3,
        colour = "#222222"
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(labels = tau_state_labels) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
        values = c(
            complete = "#D9EAF7",

    )
```

The classification table retains the evidence behind those labels.

```{r pxd020717-details}
tau_details <- tau_fit$classifications[
    tau_fit$classifications$feature %in%

    c(
        "feature",

]
```

The condition-specific pattern is clearest for `MAPT_pT217`. It is absent from
all three selected control samples and detected in all three selected
Alzheimer's disease samples. The comparison below applies the same cutoff and
majority rule to the original values as one pooled block.

```{r pxd020717-pooling}
tau_pooled_values <- unname(tau_x["MAPT_pT217", ])
tau_pooled_observed <- sum(!is.na(tau_pooled_values))
tau_pooled_mean <- mean(tau_pooled_values, na.rm = TRUE)
tau_pooled_state <- if (all(!is.na(tau_pooled_values))) {
    "complete"
} else if (tau_pooled_mean < 24.5) {
    "MNAR"
} else if (tau_pooled_observed > length(tau_pooled_values) / 2) {
    "MAR"
} else {
    "insufficient"
}

tau_pt217_states <- tau_fit$classifications[
    tau_fit$classifications$feature == "MAPT_pT217",
    c("condition", "observed_count", "sample_count", "mean_intensity", "state")
]
tau_pt217_states <- tau_pt217_states[
    match(c("control", "AD"), tau_pt217_states$condition),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
tau_pooling_summary <- rbind(
    data.frame(
        scope = "Pooled original samples",
        observed_count = tau_pooled_observed,
        sample_count = length(tau_pooled_values),
        mean_intensity = tau_pooled_mean,
        state = tau_pooled_state
    ),
    data.frame(
        scope = paste(tau_pt217_states$condition, "condition"),
        observed_count = tau_pt217_states$observed_count,
        sample_count = tau_pt217_states$sample_count,
        mean_intensity = tau_pt217_states$mean_intensity,
        state = tau_pt217_states$state
    )
)
knitr::kable(
    tau_pooling_summary,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Scope", "Observed", "Samples", "Mean intensity", "State")
)
```

```{r pxd020717-check, include=FALSE}
tau_classification_keys <- paste(
    tau_fit$classifications$feature,
    tau_fit$classifications$condition,
    sep = "::"
)
tau_state_lookup <- stats::setNames(
    as.character(tau_fit$classifications$state),
    tau_classification_keys
)
tau_retained_lookup <- stats::setNames(
    tau_fit$feature_status$retained,
    tau_fit$feature_status$feature
)
stopifnot(
    identical(dim(tau_x), c(7L, 6L)),
    sum(tau_fit$feature_status$retained) == 4L,
    nrow(tau_fit$seed_log) == 3L,
    identical(tau_pooled_state, "MNAR"),
    identical(
        unname(tau_state_lookup[c(
            "MAPT_pS404::control",
            "MAPT_pS404::AD",
            "MAPT_pS202::control",
            "MAPT_pS202::AD",
            "MAPT_pT217::control",
            "MAPT_pT217::AD",
            "MAPT_pT231::control",
            "MAPT_pT231::AD"
        )]),
        c("MNAR", "complete", "MAR", "MAR", "MNAR", "complete", "insufficient", "MNAR")
    ),
    identical(
        unname(tau_retained_lookup[
            c("MAPT_pS404", "MAPT_pS202", "MAPT_pT403", "MAPT_pT217", "MAPT_pT231")
        ]),
        c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
    )
)
```

The pooled pT217 block has three observations from six samples and a mean below
the cutoff, so it receives one MNAR-like label. Condition-aware classification
instead records the control block as MNAR-like, the Alzheimer's disease block
as complete, and retains the site. This is a routing example, not evidence that
missingness has a known mechanism or that pT217 differs between populations.

# Result components

- `data` - retained rows in the input representation, with recorded rescue
    values inserted.
- `classifications` - one row per feature and condition, with the values used
    for classification, the assigned state, and the retention decision.
- `groups` - retained `MNAR`, `MAR`, `complete`, and `MAR_or_complete` feature
    names for each condition.
- `feature_status` - one retention decision for every original feature.
- `cutoffs`, `cutoff_diagnostics` - condition boundaries, how they were chosen,
    method details, and warnings.
- `profiles` - feature statistics, the density grid, and smoothing details.
- `seed_log` - a record of each artificial rescue value, including rescues on
    features later dropped.
- `groups_by_sample` - aligned condition label for every output sample.
- `call` - the matched call used to create the result.

# The stored missingness profile

For each condition, ImputeFinder estimates missing and complete feature-mean
density curves on one intensity grid. If `n_1 f_1(x)` is the count-weighted
density for blocks with missing values and `n_0 f_0(x)` is the corresponding
density for complete blocks, the displayed profile is

```text
                n_1 f_1(x)
p_missing(x) = -------------------------
                n_1 f_1(x) + n_0 f_0(x)
```

This is the local proportion of incomplete feature blocks, not the average
fraction of missing samples. The feature statistics, grid, bandwidth, class
counts, warnings, and cutoff details are stored in the result. Plotting uses
those stored values directly.

```{r stored-profile}
fit$profiles$control$metadata[c("class_counts", "bandwidth", "kernel")]
head(
    fit$profiles$control$grid[
        , c("intensity", "missing_proportion", "supported")
    ]
)
```

```{r manual-profile, fig.cap=manual_profile_caption}
plot_missingness(fit, "control")
```

This nine-feature panel is selected to show classification rules, not to
estimate a population profile. Its curve illustrates the stored profile,
manual cutoff, and rescue value, but it is too small for automatic selection or
scientific interpretation of the transition.

# Cutoff sensitivity with known states

A prior benchmark swept the MNAR cutoff and compared downstream detection
metrics. The compact experiment below applies the same sensitivity-analysis
logic to ImputeFinder's narrower package responsibility: classification. It
creates known MAR and MNAR blocks with overlapping intensity ranges, adds
complete blocks, and repeats classification at manual cutoffs from 8 to 14.
Metrics focus on the incomplete blocks because complete blocks do not use the
cutoff.

```{r cutoff-benchmark-data, include=FALSE}
make_benchmark_block <- function(
    means,
    observed_count,
    sample_count = 6L
) {
    block <- matrix(
        NA_real_,
        nrow = length(means),
        ncol = sample_count
    )
    offsets <- seq(-0.15, 0.15, length.out = observed_count)

    for (feature_index in seq_along(means)) {
        observed <- (
            feature_index - 1L + seq_len(observed_count) - 1L
        ) %% sample_count + 1L
        block[feature_index, observed] <-
            means[[feature_index]] + offsets
    }
    block
}

features_per_state <- 120L
benchmark_mnar <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(8.5, 12.4, length.out = features_per_state),
    observed_count = 2L
)
benchmark_mar <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(11.6, 15.5, length.out = features_per_state),
    observed_count = 4L
)
benchmark_complete <- make_benchmark_block(
    seq(9, 16, length.out = 60L),
    observed_count = 6L
)
cutoff_benchmark_x <- rbind(
    benchmark_mnar,
    benchmark_mar,
    benchmark_complete
)
rownames(cutoff_benchmark_x) <- c(
    sprintf("mnar_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_mnar))),
    sprintf("mar_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_mar))),
    sprintf("complete_%03d", seq_len(nrow(benchmark_complete)))
)
colnames(cutoff_benchmark_x) <- paste0(
    "benchmark_sample_",
    seq_len(ncol(cutoff_benchmark_x))
)
cutoff_benchmark_truth <- setNames(
    c(
        rep("MNAR", nrow(benchmark_mnar)),
        rep("MAR", nrow(benchmark_mar)),
        rep("complete", nrow(benchmark_complete))
    ),
    rownames(cutoff_benchmark_x)
)

cutoff_benchmark_fits <- lapply(8:14, function(cutoff) {
    classify_missingness(
        cutoff_benchmark_x,
        group = rep("benchmark", ncol(cutoff_benchmark_x)),
        cutoffs = c(benchmark = cutoff),
        seed = 1L
    )
})
names(cutoff_benchmark_fits) <- as.character(8:14)
cutoff_benchmark_metrics <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(8:14, function(cutoff) {
        benchmark_fit <- cutoff_benchmark_fits[[as.character(cutoff)]]
        prediction <- setNames(
            as.character(benchmark_fit$classifications$state),
            benchmark_fit$classifications$feature
        )
        prediction <- prediction[names(cutoff_benchmark_truth)]
        mnar_recall <- mean(
            prediction[cutoff_benchmark_truth == "MNAR"] == "MNAR"
        )
        mar_recall <- mean(
            prediction[cutoff_benchmark_truth == "MAR"] == "MAR"
        )

        data.frame(
            cutoff = cutoff,
            metric = c(
                "MNAR recall",
                "MAR recall",
                "Balanced accuracy"
            ),
            value = c(
                mnar_recall,
                mar_recall,
                mean(c(mnar_recall, mar_recall))
            ),
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
    })
)
cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric <- factor(
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric,
    levels = c("MNAR recall", "MAR recall", "Balanced accuracy")
)
balanced_accuracy <- cutoff_benchmark_metrics[
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric == "Balanced accuracy",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(identical(
    balanced_accuracy$cutoff[which.max(balanced_accuracy$value)],
    12L
))
```

```{r cutoff-benchmark-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.8, fig.cap=cutoff_benchmark_caption}
ggplot2::ggplot(
    cutoff_benchmark_metrics,
    ggplot2::aes(x = cutoff, y = value)
) +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 12,
        linetype = 2,
        colour = "#555555"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#2C7FB8") +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.3, colour = "#2C7FB8") +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(metric), nrow = 1) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 8:14) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 1),
        breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
        labels = function(value) paste0(round(value * 100), "%")
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Manual cutoff", y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
        panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(
            fill = "#F2F2F2",
            colour = NA
        ),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
    )
```

Lower cutoffs favour MAR recall and higher cutoffs favour MNAR recall. Balanced
accuracy peaks at the design boundary, but the overlapping distributions prevent
perfect separation. This is a controlled classification benchmark. It does not
establish a universal cutoff or measure downstream imputation and differential
analysis performance.

```{r cutoff-confusion-heatmap, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.5, fig.cap=confusion_caption}
confusion_truth <- cutoff_benchmark_truth[cutoff_benchmark_truth != "complete"]
confusion_states <- c("MNAR", "MAR", "insufficient")
cutoff_confusion <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(10L, 12L, 14L), function(cutoff) {
    classifications <- cutoff_benchmark_fits[[as.character(cutoff)]]$classifications
    predicted <- setNames(as.character(classifications$state), classifications$feature)
    predicted <- predicted[names(confusion_truth)]
    stopifnot(!anyNA(predicted), all(predicted %in% confusion_states))
    counts <- table(
        truth = factor(confusion_truth, levels = c("MNAR", "MAR")),
        predicted = factor(predicted, levels = confusion_states)
    )
    recalls <- cutoff_benchmark_metrics[
        cutoff_benchmark_metrics$cutoff == cutoff &
            cutoff_benchmark_metrics$metric != "Balanced accuracy", "value"
    ]
    stopifnot(
        all(rowSums(counts) == features_per_state),
        isTRUE(all.equal(
            unname(c(counts["MNAR", "MNAR"], counts["MAR", "MAR"])) /
                features_per_state,
            recalls, tolerance = 1e-12
        )),
        !any(classifications$retained[classifications$state %in% c("MNAR", "insufficient")])
    )
    cells <- as.data.frame(counts, responseName = "count")
    cells$fraction <- cells$count / features_per_state
    cells$cutoff <- paste("Cutoff", cutoff)
    cells
}))
cutoff_confusion$truth <- factor(cutoff_confusion$truth, levels = c("MAR", "MNAR"))
ggplot2::ggplot(cutoff_confusion,
    ggplot2::aes(x = predicted, y = truth, fill = fraction)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%d\n(%.1f%%)", count, 100 * fraction),
            colour = fraction > 0.55), size = 3.1
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(cutoff), nrow = 1L) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(labels = c(MNAR = "MNAR", MAR = "MAR",
        insufficient = "Insufficient")) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#222222", `TRUE` = "white"),
        guide = "none") +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F7FBFF", high = "#08519C",
        limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("0%", "50%", "100%"),
        name = "Within-truth fraction") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Classifier label before filtering", y = "Known design state") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
        strip.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#F2F2F2", colour = NA),
        strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"))

stopifnot(sum(cutoff_confusion$count) == 3L * length(confusion_truth))
```

The confusion heatmaps expose the errors behind the recall curves. A low cutoff
can label sparse MNAR-designed blocks `insufficient`, while a high cutoff can
label MAR-designed blocks `MNAR`. These are classifications before filtering.
In this one-condition benchmark, every MNAR-labelled feature is subsequently
dropped by the all-MNAR rule. State recall therefore does not measure retention.

# Automatic cutoffs

Manual cutoffs are useful when domain knowledge or a predeclared analysis fixes
the boundary. With `cutoffs = NULL`, the default, ImputeFinder searches each
incomplete condition's profile for the lower, right-hand boundary of its main
downward transition. Conditions with no missing observations need no cutoff. A
partial named vector is also valid; automatic selection fills only the omitted
conditions.

The deterministic synthetic matrix below contains two clear but different
transitions. It uses a fixed mix of incomplete and complete features so the
vignette gives the same result every time it is built.

```{r automatic-data}
make_condition <- function(n, left, right, score_offset = 0L) {
    index <- seq_len(n)
    means <- qnorm((index - 0.5) / n, mean = 12.5, sd = 2.4)
    score <- (((index + score_offset) * 104729) %% 1000003) / 1000003
    ramp <- pmin(pmax((right - means) / (right - left), 0), 1)
    missing_probability <- 1 - (1 - 0.05) * (1 - 0.68 * ramp)
    missing <- score < missing_probability

    block <- matrix(rep(means, 4L), nrow = n)
    block[cbind(which(missing), rep(4L, sum(missing)))] <- NA_real_
    block
}

feature_count <- 200L
automatic_x <- cbind(
    make_condition(feature_count, left = 10.2, right = 11),
    make_condition(feature_count, left = 13.2, right = 14, score_offset = 37L)
)
rownames(automatic_x) <- sprintf("protein_%04d", seq_len(feature_count))
colnames(automatic_x) <- paste0("automatic_sample_", seq_len(ncol(automatic_x)))
automatic_condition <- rep(c("control", "treated"), each = 4)
```

```{r automatic-fit}
automatic_fit <- classify_missingness(
    automatic_x,
    group = automatic_condition
)
round(automatic_fit$cutoffs, 3)
vapply(
    automatic_fit$cutoff_diagnostics,
    function(diagnostic) diagnostic$source,
    character(1)
)
automatic_fit$cutoff_diagnostics$control$method
```

```{r automatic-profile, fig.cap=automatic_profile_caption}
plot_missingness(automatic_fit, "control")
```

An automatic estimate is returned only when there are enough complete and
incomplete features, enough support across the intensity range, a decreasing
missingness trend, and a clear transition. Flat, missing-only, sparse, or
ambiguous profiles raise a condition-specific `imputefinder_cutoff_error` with
the profile and diagnostic attached. Complete-only conditions need no cutoff.
Inspect the stored profile and supply a named manual cutoff when automatic
estimation fails.

# Filtered data and downstream branches

`fit$data` contains only retained features and includes their logged rescue
anchors. `seed_log` also audits pre-filter rescues on features later dropped.
`fit$groups` divides the retained rows independently within each condition into
`MNAR`, `MAR`, `complete`, and the combined `MAR_or_complete` group.

The intended order is:

1. classify the unnormalised log2 matrix;
2. normalise the entire returned `fit$data` object with the method chosen for
    the experiment;
3. split samples by `fit$groups_by_sample`;
4. within each condition, apply an MNAR method only to its `MNAR` rows and a
    MAR method only to its `MAR_or_complete` rows;
5. recombine conditions in original sample order.

The following code performs the split and stops before normalisation or
imputation, because those choices depend on the analysis and are not
ImputeFinder dependencies.

```{r downstream-branches}
split_condition <- function(result, condition_name) {
    samples <- names(result$groups_by_sample)[
        result$groups_by_sample == condition_name
    ]
    condition_data <- result$data[, samples, drop = FALSE]

    list(
        MNAR = condition_data[
            result$groups[[condition_name]]$MNAR,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ],
        MAR_or_complete = condition_data[
            result$groups[[condition_name]]$MAR_or_complete,
            ,
            drop = FALSE
        ]
    )
}

downstream <- lapply(names(fit$groups), function(condition_name) {
    split_condition(fit, condition_name)
})
names(downstream) <- names(fit$groups)

vapply(downstream, function(branch) nrow(branch$MNAR), integer(1))
vapply(downstream, function(branch) nrow(branch$MAR_or_complete), integer(1))
c(
    on_off_in_control_MNAR =
        "condition_on_off" %in% rownames(downstream$control$MNAR),
    on_off_in_treated_MAR_or_complete =
        "condition_on_off" %in%
            rownames(downstream$treated$MAR_or_complete),
    mixed_in_control_MNAR =
        "mixed_mechanism" %in% rownames(downstream$control$MNAR),
    mixed_in_treated_MAR_or_complete =
        "mixed_mechanism" %in%
            rownames(downstream$treated$MAR_or_complete)
)
```

## An illustrative routing manifest

Suppose the analysis plan assigns an MNAR-aware method to low-intensity blocks,
a MAR-aware method to supported incomplete blocks, and no replacement to
complete blocks. The selected algorithms remain external to ImputeFinder. The
classification table can express that plan as a condition-specific manifest.

```{r routing-manifest}
manifest_features <- c(
    "condition_on_off",
    "differential_mar",
    "mixed_mechanism"
)
routing_manifest <- fit$classifications[
    fit$classifications$retained &
        fit$classifications$feature %in% manifest_features,
    c("feature", "condition", "observed_count", "missing_count", "state")
]
routing_manifest <- routing_manifest[
    order(
        match(routing_manifest$feature, manifest_features),
        match(routing_manifest$condition, unique(condition))
    ),
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
rownames(routing_manifest) <- NULL

pipeline_actions <- c(
    MNAR = "send to the MNAR branch",
    MAR = "send to the MAR branch",
    complete = "carry forward unchanged"
)
routing_manifest$pipeline_action <- unname(
    pipeline_actions[as.character(routing_manifest$state)]
)
knitr::kable(
    routing_manifest,
    col.names = c("Feature", "Condition", "Observed", "Missing", "State", "Action")
)
```

```{r routing-manifest-check, include=FALSE}
on_off_route <- routing_manifest[
    routing_manifest$feature == "condition_on_off",
    ,
    drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(
    identical(as.character(on_off_route$state), c("MNAR", "complete")),
    identical(
        on_off_route$pipeline_action,
        c("send to the MNAR branch", "carry forward unchanged")
    )
)
```

The manifest sends `condition_on_off` and `mixed_mechanism` to the MNAR branch
only for control samples. The treated `condition_on_off` block passes through
unchanged, while treated `mixed_mechanism` enters the MAR branch.
`differential_mar` enters the MAR branch in both conditions.

After branch outputs are recombined, `condition_on_off` remains available to a
condition-comparison model. A pooled classifier would have dropped it before
normalisation or imputation. The manifest records each block's state and
destination, while `fit$classifications` retains the supporting evidence.
Together they support review and reproducible reruns.

Complete blocks need no replacement. Grouping them with MAR rows supplies a
single non-MNAR branch while preserving each explicit `complete` state in the
classification table.

# `SummarizedExperiment` input

A `SummarizedExperiment` uses the same matrix core. Select the condition column
explicitly and name the assay whenever the object contains more than one. The
returned `data` preserves the representation, unselected assays, row and column
metadata, and sample order while filtering rows and replacing only the selected
assay with the seed-modified values.

```{r summarized-experiment}
se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = list(log2_intensity = x),
    colData = data.frame(
        condition = condition,
        row.names = colnames(x)
    )
)
fit_se <- classify_missingness(
    se,
    group_col = "condition",
    assay = "log2_intensity",
    cutoffs = c(control = 12, treated = 12)
)
identical(
    SummarizedExperiment::assay(fit_se$data, "log2_intensity"),
    fit$data
)
```

# Limitations

- The cutoff is a model assumption. Biology, acquisition, and preprocessing can
    produce patterns without one descending intensity transition.
- Automatic breakpoint selection needs both incomplete and complete features.
    When the data do not support a clear transition, use a manual cutoff.
- Arithmetic means are sensitive to strong observations by design.
- Rescue anchors are artificial values. Preserve `seed_log` with the analysis
    and assess their influence downstream.
- Classification is heuristic. ImputeFinder does not prove mechanisms, choose
    an imputation algorithm, or validate the final biological analysis.

The test suite covers intensity-independent MAR,
intensity-dependent MNAR, condition-specific on/off features, several group
sizes and cutoffs, rescue seeds, and name permutations. These tests cover those
cases but do not establish performance for every proteomics experiment.
